note: Monophenolase reaction of tyrosinase. Rhea writes L-tyrosine + O2 = L-dopaquinone + H2O as one reaction: free L-DOPA is not a product (pathway review, O7). Rhea lists the zwitterions CHEBI:58315 and CHEBI:57924; mapped to the neutral parents. KEGG KO K00505 is a cross-reference of the step. Small molecules (O2, H2O, CO2, H+, ATP, AMP, diphosphate, acceptor) are not listed as participants.

Diphenolase reaction of tyrosinase (2 L-dopa + O2 = 2 L-dopaquinone + 2 H2O). L-DOPA is a substrate here; no reaction of the table makes it. Rhea lists the zwitterions CHEBI:57504 and CHEBI:57924; mapped to the neutral parents. Small molecules (O2, H2O, CO2, H+, ATP, AMP, diphosphate, acceptor) are not listed as participants.

Curated: oxidation of exogenous L-DOPA to L-dopaquinone by a laccase. Rhea has only the generic laccase reaction RHEA:11276 (4 hydroquinone + O2 = 4 benzosemiquinone + 2 H2O, EC 1.10.3.2), whose participants are compound classes. The product is written as the quinone, as in the abstract of PMID 8760791 (L-dopa 'to quinones, which then polymerize to melanin'); the semiquinone step is not shown. RHEA:34287 has the same net equation and is the tyrosinase reaction (EC 1.14.18.1); the two are kept apart so that no laccase is linked to a tyrosinase reaction. In the reference organism the substrate is exogenous: Cryptococcus neoformans produces melanin only from exogenous substrates (PMID 17098915). KEGG KO K00421 and K05909 are cross-references of the step. Small molecules (O2, H2O, CO2, H+, ATP, AMP, diphosphate, acceptor) are not listed as participants.

Curated: oxidation of exogenous dopamine to decarboxy dopachrome by the Cryptococcus laccase (mass spectrometry, PMID 8300520). The name 'decarboxy dopachrome' of the abstract is mapped by the curator to dopaminechrome (keto form), CHEBI:189002 (C8H7NO2, the formula of L-dopachrome minus CO2); PROPOSED. The steps between dopamine and dopaminechrome are not shown in the abstract. Rhea has only the generic laccase reaction RHEA:11276 (4 hydroquinone + O2 = 4 benzosemiquinone + 2 H2O, EC 1.10.3.2), whose participants are compound classes. Small molecules (O2, H2O, CO2, H+, ATP, AMP, diphosphate, acceptor) are not listed as participants.

Curated: laccase-dependent pigment formation from exogenous homogentisic acid in Cryptococcus neoformans (PMID 17098915). The pigment has no formula, so no product is listed. The abstract does not name the laccase gene. Rhea has only the generic laccase reaction RHEA:11276 (4 hydroquinone + O2 = 4 benzosemiquinone + 2 H2O, EC 1.10.3.2), whose participants are compound classes.

Curated, non-enzymatic in this table: L-dopaquinone to L-dopachrome. No enzyme link above T4. UniProt states for the Agaricus bisporus tyrosinases (C7FF04, function text) that the o-quinones 'evolve spontaneously' to pigment intermediates. The single line from L-dopaquinone to L-dopachrome is a simplification: the intermediate leucodopachrome (CHEBI:60872) is not listed. The chemistry is from the design and the pathway review (RECALLED there); no abstract was read for it.

L-dopachrome to 5,6-dihydroxyindole-2-carboxylate (dopachrome tautomerase; an animal enzyme, for example human DCT, UniProt P40126). For fungi the link is T4 only: UniProt has no reviewed fungal entry with EC 5.3.3.12 (search on 2026-11-21); the unreviewed fungal entries with this EC have the automatic protein name 'L-dopachrome isomerase'. One PubMed query for a fungal dopachrome tautomerase found none. Rhea lists the anions CHEBI:57509 and CHEBI:16875; mapped to the neutral parents.

4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase. The reaction is a step of tyrosine catabolism and the source of homogentisic acid for pyomelanin. Rhea lists the anions CHEBI:36242 and CHEBI:16169; mapped to the neutral parents. KEGG KO K00457 is a cross-reference of the step. Small molecules (O2, H2O, CO2, H+, ATP, AMP, diphosphate, acceptor) are not listed as participants.

Homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase: removes homogentisic acid (tyrosine catabolism). Not a pigment-forming reaction: in Aspergillus fumigatus the hmgA deletion raises pigment formation (PMID 19028908). Rhea lists CHEBI:16169 (1-) and CHEBI:17105 (2-); mapped to the neutral parents. KEGG KO K00451 is a cross-reference of the step. Small molecules (O2, H2O, CO2, H+, ATP, AMP, diphosphate, acceptor) are not listed as participants.

Curated, no enzyme link: oxidation and polymerisation of homogentisic acid to pyomelanin. The pigment has no formula, so no product is listed. The abstract of PMID 9570125 calls it spontaneous (homogentisic acid made by a fungal HPPD in Escherichia coli); in Aspergillus fumigatus the accumulation of homogentisic acid raises pigment formation (PMID 19028908). Whether a fungal enzyme takes part was not checked.

Aspulvinone E synthesis from two molecules of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate by an NRPS-like enzyme. Rhea has no EC for this reaction. Rhea lists the anions CHEBI:36242 and CHEBI:58240; mapped to the neutral parents. Small molecules (O2, H2O, CO2, H+, ATP, AMP, diphosphate, acceptor) are not listed as participants.
